A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–N. Textual and visual inspection supports a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gridworld and Sepsis simulation results in Section 6, with additional intervention, estimation-error, and robustness experiments in Appendices K–M.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Gridworld and Sepsis results, including the supplementary experiments in Appendices K–M.

M1.justification: The TCFE decomposition, ASE-SV agent attribution, r-SSE-ICC state attribution, and posterior-sampling Algorithm 1 are retained. No algorithm step, objective, or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gridworld delivery task with an LLM planner and two RL actors, and the same clinician–AI Sepsis simulator. Intervention scenarios and appendix evaluation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Both retain comparisons with individual agent-specific effects, the same alternative effect decompositions, and the ground-truth checks in Appendix L. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 6.2's Gini footnote changes the reported selection rule from post-intervention states to post-intervention states corresponding to AI turns. This is a limited revision of the stated evaluation protocol; the unchanged plots do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The sparsity analysis, Planner-intervention case study, estimation-error checks, and noise-ordering robustness experiments retain the same questions and evidence. The added sampling caveat does not supply a new error analysis.

E5.justification: Both report Gridworld averages and standard errors over five seeds and Sepsis estimation-error distributions over ten seeds. Repeated-run counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result plots and substantive experimental findings are retained, including the 82% counterfactual treatment-success probability and discrepancies of up to 95% between summed individual effects and total ASE. Figure 6's exclusion disclosure accompanies unchanged plotted results.

T1.justification: The effect definitions, attribution axioms, noise-monotonicity assumption, theorems, and proofs are retained. Structural-function notation is simplified, and Appendix C explicitly applies the existing consistency conditions at every time step; no substantive mathematical result changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and Discussion retain the same decomposition, attribution, novelty, and interpretability claims. The new Impact Statement restates the existing accountability application.

C2.justification: Appendix K.2 newly explains that finite sampling can produce erroneous negative contribution estimates and states that these cases were excluded from the plots. This adds a substantive qualification to the state-attribution evidence.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an explicit code-repository address in the introduction and Appendix I.3, replacing v2's Supplemental Material reference for runtime details. Appendix K.2 also newly documents the exclusion of negative estimates from Figure 6.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to mediation analysis, agent-specific effects, intrinsic causal contributions, and Shapley attribution are unchanged. The bibliography is reflowed without adding or removing works.

P1.justification: Section headings and example prose receive small edits. v3 adds an Impact Statement and Acknowledgements and replaces the preprint notice with publication details, while retaining the main narrative and appendix organization.

P2.justification: Added footnotes and end matter cause limited page and column reflow, and Figure 6's caption receives small wording edits. All ten figures and three tables remain without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: Explicit code access instructions and clearer reporting of the Gini state selection and excluded negative estimates modestly improve reproducibility and transparency. The scientific evidence is retained. The number and impact of excluded cases remain unspecified, so the improvement is limited.
